correctness.rationale: Rank-one kernels of the oblique projection factors force exactly one rank loss per row; because n losses are necessary and sufficient for zero first-sweep error, every KO direction must be orthogonal to all previous rows. This gives the explicit chain Gram identity, equivalent by positive-definite bidiagonal factorization to tridiagonal precision. The n=3 Schur complement derives the operator norm with strict positivity bounds. The proof addresses n>=2, all invertible real A, all initial errors and right-hand sides, and precisely excludes threshold-skipped and finite-precision cases. The actual CHECK.py uses exact fractions to test both statements and exercises boundary cases.
